skill.name: mo-qa
skill.description: Use Momentic's `mo` CLI to run and control Mo, Momentic's cloud autonomous QA agent. Start and monitor QA sessions, handle follow-up input, manage tunnels, and transfer approved test artifacts.
skill.summary: Run and manage Momentic Mo sessions for controlled web application QA.
skill.author: momentic-ai

security_audit.summary: The static catalog is mostly false positive matches from Markdown command examples, CLI names, paths, and documented credential handling. The remote installer uses a critical curl-to-shell pattern, and the skill also enables remote execution and file transfer that require strict scope and data controls.

remediation.issue: The installation guide pipes a remote script directly from curl into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Publish signed binaries or packages, or download the installer first and verify its checksum or signature before execution.

remediation.issue: Files can be uploaded to a hosted sandbox and later downloaded locally.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval, document data classification rules, and prohibit credentials, production exports, and sensitive files unless the user authorizes them.

remediation.issue: Mo can run browser, network, code, and shell actions, including destructive actions when the brief invites them.
remediation.suggestion: Use isolated staging targets, least-privilege accounts, explicit destructive-action confirmation, and narrow tunnel allowlists for every session.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Agent Execution Scope
semantic_findings.description: Mo runs in a hosted sandbox and can inspect network traffic, run code and shell commands, and delegate exploration. A broad or untrusted QA brief could cause actions beyond the intended test scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The capability and the instruction that destructive actions may occur when invited are stated directly. The risk depends on the target and brief, so this is a contextual control finding rather than proof of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Artifact Transfer
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to upload local files to Mo's hosted sandbox and download artifacts back. Uploading an unintended fixture, credential, or production file could disclose sensitive data to the service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The transfer behavior and remote destination are explicit. The example uses a fixture, so the finding identifies a plausible data-handling risk rather than evidence that sensitive data is currently exfiltrated.

content.user_title: Run Controlled Web QA with Mo
content.value_statement: Manual web QA can be slow to repeat and difficult to observe across browser states. This skill helps you create, monitor, and manage Momentic Mo sessions with explicit test scope.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the Mo CLI is installed and directs users to authentication or installation references.
Builds structured QA briefs with targets, expected behavior, test data rules, and acceptance criteria.
Starts Mo sessions and captures session identifiers and web URLs for follow-up work.
Polls status and transcripts while inspecting structured test cases, bugs, controls, and verdicts.
Continues, stops, or archives sessions with documented wait and state-handling behavior.
Starts narrow tunnels and transfers approved files between the local machine and Mo's hosted sandbox.
limitations: It does not execute Mo commands or complete QA work without user-run CLI actions.
It does not create credentials, test accounts, test data permissions, or acceptance criteria.
It cannot change concurrency settings on an existing session.
It depends on Momentic service availability, authentication, and network access.

use_cases.title: Validate a Staging Release
use_cases.description: Prepare a focused brief, run Mo against a staging URL, and review structured results before a release decision.

use_cases.title: Test a Private Local Build
use_cases.description: Expose only required local or private addresses through a tunnel, then connect the Mo session to that tunnel.

use_cases.title: Manage Long-Running QA Work
use_cases.description: Poll visible session state, answer pending questions, stop active work, or archive completed sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic QA Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a QA brief for this staging URL: [URL]. Test [change]. Use [account]. Create only [test data]. Do not perform [restricted actions]. Pass when [criteria].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define the minimum scope for one staging workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Local Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the exact local host and port needed for this flow: [flow]. Draft the narrow tunnel command and a QA brief. Use only the staging account and fixture data. Include cleanup steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test a private build with limited network exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Review Session Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: For session [session ID], specify a bounded polling sequence. Compare status and read state, inspect test cases, bugs, controls, and verdicts, and identify when user input is required.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: monitor an active session without losing fast responses.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Follow-Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this session state: [state and pending input], draft the next Mo message with --wait. Preserve the original acceptance criteria, avoid destructive actions, and state what must be verified afterward.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: continue a session while preserving authorization boundaries.

output_examples.input: Test the checkout shipping change on staging. Do not submit payment or modify shared catalog data.
output_examples.output: A scoped QA brief covering the target URL, expected shipping behavior, staging sign-in, test-cart limits, prohibited actions, and pass criteria.

output_examples.input: Mo is waiting for input after reporting a possible checkout bug.
output_examples.output: A follow-up message that answers the pending question, preserves the staging-only scope, and requests bounded waiting for the next attention boundary.

output_examples.input: The local app needs one API address and one web address.
output: A tunnel plan exposing only the two required host and port addresses.
A reminder to stop the tunnel after the final session.

best_practices: Define the target, expected behavior, test data, prohibited actions, and acceptance criteria before starting.
Use staging accounts and fixture data, and review structured findings before reporting a defect.
Expose only required tunnel addresses and stop tunnels after the final session.
anti_patterns: Starting a session with invented credentials, permissions, test data, or acceptance criteria.
Uploading credentials or sensitive production files to the hosted sandbox.
Sending a new turn to change concurrency or inviting destructive actions without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It provides operating guidance for starting and managing Momentic Mo sessions for controlled web application QA.

faq.question: Does the skill run the CLI automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and decision guidance for a user or agent that can run the Mo CLI.

faq.question: What should a QA brief include?
faq.answer: Include the exact target, expected behavior, sign-in method, test data rules, prohibited actions, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Can Mo test a local application?
faq.answer: Yes. Start a tunnel for only the required local or private addresses and pass its tunnel identifier to the session.

faq.question: How should session output be reviewed?
faq.answer: Inspect status, transcript state, test cases, bugs, controls, and verdicts before deciding whether a test passed.

faq.question: How should files be handled?
faq.answer: Transfer only approved fixture files. Never upload credentials or sensitive production data without explicit authorization and appropriate controls.
